title: Etale-local logarithmic lifts through a log fibre product
statement: Let $p:X'\to X$, $q:X'\to Y'$, $f:X\to Y$ and $h:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary log maps [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation], with composites as in [lem-sfb-log-morphism-operations]. Suppose $f\circ p=h\circ q$, and the square has the universal factorization property for all test log structures [lem-sfb-strict-log-pullback-universal]. If $f$ has etale-local infinitesimal lifts [def-sfb-log-infinitesimal-lifting-properties], then so does $q$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.5--3.3.6, p.107; X 1.2, pp.136--139. Explicit pairing-of-lifts argument by F3.

proof.text: Project a strict fine square-zero test for q along p and h. Associativity and the square equation make it a test for f. Use the local lifting property of f, keeping exactly its etale neighbourhood, restricted log structures, strict etale restriction maps and test immersion.

Pair the chosen lift to X with the fixed neighbourhood map to Yprime by the log pullback property. Its projection to Yprime is the required bottom map. Its restriction to the test thickening equals the prescribed top map because both projections agree; uniqueness in the same product property gives equality. This supplies every witness in the local lifting predicate.
